maria: Bringing up hf/forge-7b on staging — tokenizer weirdness: lots of '<|eot|>' and '�' appearing mid-sentence after conversion. Anyone seen this after HF -> Redwood converter?

alex: which tokenizer object? sentencepiece or byte-level BPE?

maria: it's ByteLevelBPET. From HF artifacts: tokenizer.json + merges.txt + special_tokens_map.json. snippet:
```
{
  "eot_token": "<|eot|>",
  "additional_special_tokens": ["<|eot|>"]
}
```
conversion log attached: `convert-tool v1.9.2` — seemed to run ok.

sam: could be normalizer differences. HF tokenizers often run NFKC or NFC depending on the model. Redwood pretokenizer applies NFC by default. Ligatures/combining marks can float.

jin: yep. quick check: run `python -c \"from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json').pre_tokenizer)\"` — does it show a Normalizer step?

maria: ran that, HF normalizer shows `NFKC` in config, converter didn't preserve it.

alex: ah — converter historically strips HF normalizer and relies on runtime normalizer. If converter maps HF normalizer -> redwood_normalizer incorrectly, special tokens like `<|eot|>` can get re-normalized into byte fallbacks.

maria: example input -> output:
```
Input: "Hello<|eot|> world"
HF tokens: ["Hello", "<|eot|>", " world"]
Redwood tokens: ["Hello", "<|eot|>", " �", " world"]
```

sam: that replacement char suggests byte-fallback kicked in when token bytes didn't map after normalization. Also check leading/trailing spaces handling — ByteLevel often uses `add_prefix_space` semantics.

jin: can you dump `special_tokens_map.json` from the converted package? converter might have turned `<|eot|>` into two tokens if a zero-width joiner/norm changed bytes.

maria: here: `{"eot":"<|eot|>"}` — converter produced this. I suspect the order of normalizer -> pretokenizer got swapped.

alex: short-term fix: run converter with `--preserve-normalizer` or patch converted tokenizer.json to include the HF normalizer block. That should keep `<|eot|>` intact.

maria: trying now with `redwood-convert --preserve-normalizer --write-tokenizer` ; will report.

ops-bot: conversion job #424 finished: success=false, logs=/internal/logs/424

sam: follow-up: add a unit test in onboarding pipeline that tokenizes a set of special-token heavy prompts (emoji, ligatures, combined accents) and compares HF vs Redwood token sequences — fail fast.

maria: agreed. I'll add tests and a small fix to converter. If that works we'll re-run quantization experiments — can't trust bpe alignments otherwise.

jin: also note chat template differences: HF chat templates sometimes expect leading space before user turns; check `chat_formatting` mapping in model card.

alex: good call. these small differences silently change token counts -> can affect perf/quality after quant/kv-cache offsets.

maria: ok pushed preserve-normalizer patch to staging conversion, re-converting now. thanks all :tada:

alex: :thumbsup:
